title: What permutation contact remembers: loops, nerves and knots among loops
claim: (1) A loop of permutation contact closes exactly when the composed permutation has a fixed point, and a bouquet of loops with one selector each allows a selector pattern exactly when the selected holonomies share a fixed point. (2) The selector shape (free-set complex) is the nerve of the holonomies' fixed-point sets, and a minimal non-face is excluded alone, so a minimal non-face of three or more loops is a knot (K1-K3). (3) Free contact never binds two loops. (4) A knot among k >= 1 loops needs at least k+1 witness values, and the star transpositions on k+1 values are one. (5) Every simplicial complex is the nerve of the fixed-point sets of a family of involutions. (1)-(5) are kernel-checked in Lean. In prose: a connected network of permutation contact allows a pattern exactly when its holonomy group has a common fixed point; for free abelian contact this is the vanishing of a class in H^1(G; Gamma); with uniform group contact the allowed fraction depends on the network only through its number of independent loops.
failure_conditions: The kernel rejects the file, or a stated theorem depends on an axiom other than propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
A control that alters a statement (k values instead of k+1 for the star, a bound of k+2, a knot under free contact, a nerve of sets that are not down-closed) is accepted.
The theorems disagree with the exact census HOLES-COHOMOLOGY-20261019-001A-E001 on its cases.
foundation_claim_scope: What a network of permutation contact keeps once its witnesses are forgotten, and when its loops bind into ties and knots. No native recurrence, composed topology, path, metric, space or physical claim; the networks are laid out by hand.

validation.novelty: known-overlap-likely for the loop, bouquet and network rules (bijection constraints, label-extended covering), H^1 of graphs and nerves of set families; elementary and not found stated: knots among loops are atoms, a knot among k loops needs k+1 values with stars attaining it, and selector shapes are nerves of fixed-point sets. The program's reading is new: free contact records loops one by one, and only contact with fixed points binds loops, into atoms.
